note: Format-adherence tasks for scripts/measure/grammar-test.py. Each task pairs a small JSON schema (a subset of JSON Schema) with the instruction the model is given, plus hand-written good/bad answers that --selftest uses to prove the validator accepts the good and rejects the bad without a model. The idea of a grammar benchmark follows egavrin/deal-llm-grammar-benchmark; the schemas, the validator and the tasks here are original to this repository.

tasks.instruction: Return ONE JSON object describing a made-up software engineer: keys `name` (string), `age` (integer 0-150), `skills` (array of at least 2 strings). No other keys. Output only the JSON, no prose.
Given the sentence 'the build passed on CI', return ONE JSON object with `verdict` (exactly one of "pass", "fail", "skip") and `confidence` (number 0.0-1.0). No other keys. Output only the JSON.
Return ONE JSON array of exactly 2 arrays, each holding exactly 2 integers (a 2x2 matrix). No prose, JSON only.
